articleTitle: Design rules and realisation of coplanar circuits for communication applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: Advances in the design and realisation of microwave coplanar integrated circuits are reported on. During the last years coplanar integrated circuits have become more and more interesting and they have originally been thought to be especially suited for millimetre-wave applications. But the design of microwave and millimetre-wave coplanar circuits was always a difficult task because design rules for the component- and circuit-design had not been available. In this paper it will be shown that the situation has changed in the mean time, i.e. that design tools have been developed and that additionally coplanar circuits now also are interesting for low frequency applications, e.g. in the mobile communication technique. The basis and the properties of the new available design tools for coplanar circuits will be discussed demonstrating interesting applications and several circuits for communication applications in the 1 to 40 GHz range.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coplanar waveguide filters: new design data and case studies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: The use of coplanar waveguide (CPW) has been limited by the availability of design data, especially for discontinuities and other special structures such as interdigital capacitors. Such data must be in a form simple enough to incorporate in CAD packages, which analyze designs purely in circuit terms. Accurate models of this kind are particularly important in filter design, an application for which experience with CPW elements is very limited. This paper presents some case studies of a variety of CWP filters designed using extensive design data for the discontinuities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: An inductively and capacitively loaded coplanar waveguide structure is proposed to produce a slow-wave effect. The effect is measured using resonator technique and a reduction factor of 1.8 in phase velocity has been obtained using the particular circuit given. The loaded structure has also been shown experimentally to have less radiation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical applications of CPW in radar and electronic warfare sub systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: Making CPW elements behave more like ideal distributed elements, enabled standard CAD software to be used by CWP designers. This approach also allowed new designs to be realized either in coplanar waveguide or microstrip with very little modification, increasing the usefulness of the design effort. Another benefit of this approach was that it gave CPW designers access to a large historical microstrip, design database. The design and layout rules focus mainly on preserving equipotential ground planes throughout the circuit, which is necessary to avoid unwanted modes of propagation and standing waves. It is easy to produce slot modes in CPW and they can readily propagate in poorly designed circuits. The rest of the rules cover tuning techniques, tuning circuits and fault finding techniques, which is particularly important in large integrated assemblies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Activities on coplanar waveguide structures and circuits at the IMST
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: Various numerical techniques have been applied towards such structures and numerous hybrids and MMICs have been designed utilising coplanar waveguide structures. In January 1993, most of the activities started at the University of Duisburg were focused and re-organised within the IMST (Institut fur Mobil und Satellitenfunktechnik). This paper gives today's state-of-the-art in CAD, numerical analysis and circuit design of coplanar structures within the IMST. There is also a strong CPW circuit design activity at the IMST.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coplanar resonators fabricated from thin film high-T/sub c/ superconductors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: The discovery of superconductors with transition temperatures T/sub c/ above the boiling point of liquid nitrogen (77.4 K) has opened up the real possibility of practical superconducting microwave applications, utilising the very low surface resistance R/sub s/ of the superconductor. As part of a broad research effort on novel superconducting microwave devices, the authors have used the coplanar resonator geometry to assess the microwave properties of thin films of YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7/ ('YBCO', with T/sub c/ approximately=90 K), in particular the microwave dissipation of the material at patterned film edges which dominates the performance of any planar device. The coplanar resonator is an ideal test structure since only one film surface is required before patterning (thus removing the need for double-sided deposition) in addition, microwave current densities are very high at the film edges, allowing one to study nonlinear dissipation due to high microwave power levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Full-wave characterization and CAD of CPW type MMIC components using the UNISIM electromagnetic simulator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: Following extensive efficiency and accuracy studies of direct and iterative electric field integral equation (EFIE) techniques in 1987-1989 for strip type MIC/MMIC structures, the UNISIM unified strip/CPW (coplanar waveguide) electromagnetic simulator was completed in early 1990 to cover slot and CPW type structures in addition. While first systematic numerical approaches to rigorous full-wave CPW structure characterization became available on mainframes, UNISIM is an electromagnetic tool written for use on modern desktop computers in the context of an interactive linear/nonlinear MIC/MMIC design package. Its unified strip/CPW structure simulation capabilities and its high computational efficiency are due to solving microstrip problems in terms of the unknown strip current density distribution J/sub s/ (EFIE), while treating CPW configurations in terms of the slot field E/sub s/ (dual IE). In its details, it uses advanced numerical techniques generalized and adapted to include CPW and BCPW (bridged CPW) components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer evaluation of equivalent circuit of coplanar waveguide T-junction
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: For some of its advantages, the coplanar waveguide (CPW) is preferred to the microstrip line in developing monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) on GaAs and InP. However, due to lack of powerful design software, the potentials of this line have not been fully exploited. A computer package for efficient design of a CPW circuit should contain information on the equivalent circuits of various components including bends, open and short terminations, steps etc. This paper introduces a computer technique for the determination of the equivalent circuit of the CPW-T-junction. It can be extended to find the equivalent circuits of CPW bends, terminations, steps etc. The T-junction is particularly important as it is used in the biasing of the active devices as well as in matching methods employing stubs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and characterisation of MMICs in coplanar waveguide technology up to 80 GHz
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: Coplanar waveguide technology has striking advantages for MMICs concerning process technology, because no substrate thinning or backside via hole technology is required. Better circuit performance can be achieved with CPWs compared to microstrip due to lower grounding parasitics and frequency dispersion. Based on a database of active and passive MMIC components, the authors have designed and fabricated high performance V- and W-Band MMIC amplifiers in coplanar technology which cover the 60-80 GHz frequency range. The measured and predicted MMIC results are in very good agreement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Traceability for on-wafer CPW S-parameter measurements
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Analysis, Design and Applications of Coplanar Waveguides
abstract: Formal quality systems such as the ISO 9000/BS 5750 series standards have created a growing requirement for electrical measurements to be traceable to nationally and internationally certified units such as the SI ohm, watt, and metre. For on-wafer scattering parameter measurement, results are referenced back to fundamental standards via the on-wafer impedance standards used in automatic network analyser (ANA) calibration. This paper describes work at the National Physical Laboratory towards the production of coplanar waveguide (CPW) calibration standards of certified quality on GaAs substrates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
